beta_MO_only_readout_counterexample.interpretation: The beta_MO-only posterior mean vector (and its norm) is identical in two data sets, but the Bayes factor for a model that also includes beta_RM changes. It is not sufficient for M1-vs-M2 model comparison.

binary_gaussian_data_processing.scope: exact equal-covariance Gaussian binary experiment; for general deterministic T, the KL and TV inequalities follow from data processing

no_independent_beta_MO_anchor.interpretation: beta_MO shares a constant-redshift direction with intrinsic dipole; beta_RM-beta_MO is not data-identifiable

c_optimal_redshift_shell_design.covariance: diag(sigma_stat^2/n_s) + sigma_cv^2 exp(-|z_s-z_s'|/L_corr), plus independent anchor variance sigma_anchor^2/n_anchor
c_optimal_redshift_shell_design.mean_model: g(z) beta_RM + beta_MO + d_intrinsic + c_z*z; independent low-z anchor measures beta_MO
c_optimal_redshift_shell_design.scope: one-dimensional dipole contrast design; response and covariance are synthetic; it is a method-design experiment, not an actual survey forecast

exact_common_covariance_bayes_factor_suf.common_covariance_model_family: same nuisance-integrated Cbar; all alternatives are submodels of the fixed 17D chart X; independent zero-mean Gaussian coefficient priors with fixed known variances
exact_common_covariance_bayes_factor_suf.proof_identity: q = V^{-1} m - B^{-1} b; here b=0, B=diag(THETA_STD^2), V is fixed by X,Cbar,B and independent of y

model_dependent_covariance_counterexampl.interpretation: A mean-score summary for fixed Cbar is not sufficient when a competitor changes covariance; the residual quadratic form carries model-discriminating information.

limitations: No Planck, Gaia, Quaia, NVSS, Pantheon, DESI or other real survey data are used.
The redshift response g(z)=z/(z+0.12) is a synthetic design function, not a derived physical transfer kernel.
The mock is linear-Gaussian and local; it does not establish global identifiability or Bianchi family identification.
The five readout families remain a joint posterior push-forward and must not be multiplied as independent likelihood factors.

For actual model comparison, all competitors must use the same raw observation contract or the exact model-dependent covariance/selection likelihood; source-specific transfers remain unimplemented here.
main_conclusions: For a common known covariance and candidates nested in one fixed linear chart, q=X^T C^-1(y-mu) is a common sufficient statistic for all candidate-model Bayes factors.
The complete Gaussian reference posterior mean/covariance recovers q exactly; when V is fixed, its mean alone is an invertible encoding of q.
This exact result does not extend automatically to model-dependent covariance, selection, window functions, or model-dependent summary maps.
A scalar norm is sufficient only under additional rotational symmetry of the prior and observation metric; anisotropic geometry can make direction essential.
The c-optimal redshift/anchor allocation for beta_RM-beta_MO need not coincide with a D-optimal allocation maximizing total information volume.
research_scope: tensorized posterior-pushforward T=(x,Q,Pi,F,G_F) versus physical generative theories/readout methods; no scalar-versus-tensor five-variable benchmark

scalar_norm_sufficiency_scope_test.interpretation: A scalar vector norm can be sufficient only under a symmetry-compatible model/prior/metric. Anisotropic survey geometry generally makes direction decision-relevant.
